title: 2020年12月 第1套

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Good morning.
lines.translation: 早上好 早

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My name is Paul.
lines.translation: 我叫保罗。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How can I help you today?
lines.translation: 今天有什么可以帮您的吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Morning.
lines.translation: 早 早 早 早 早 早

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I wouldn't say that it's good from where I am standing.
lines.translation: 我不会说我站的地方很好

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is Miss Wilson and this is the third time I've called this week since receiving your letter about our insurance claim.
lines.translation: 这是威尔逊小姐 这是我从收到你关于我们保险索赔的信以来 第三次打来电话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm getting a little fed up with my calls about my claim being completely disregarded.
lines.translation: 我有点厌倦我的电话 说我的要求被完全忽视了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Miss Wilson, thank you for calling back.
lines.translation: 威尔逊女士，谢谢您再次来电。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Can I take some details to help me look at your claim?
lines.translation: 我可以先记录一些信息，以便查看您的理赔情况吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's Miss May Wilson of 15 South Sea Road in Cornwall, and the details are that our village was extensively flooded 2 months ago.
lines.translation: 这是康沃尔15号南海路的May Wilson小姐 详情是两个月前我们的村庄 被广泛淹没了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water and five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.
lines.translation: 整个小屋的一楼被淹没在水里 我们五个人从那以后 一直住在一辆大篷车里

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You people are still withholding the money we are entitled to over a bizarre technical detail.
lines.translation: 你们这些人还在扣留我们应得的钱 来换取奇特的技术细节

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And it's not acceptable, Paul!
lines.translation: 这是不可接受的,保罗!

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident.
lines.translation: 威尔逊女士，根据您账户上的记录，您提到的那个荒唐的技术细节，是指在事故发生前的那个月，您没有支付房屋保险费。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you're suddenly saying that you didn't receive it on time.
lines.translation: 那笔钱已经从我们的账户里扣走了，而现在到了你们该赔付的时候，你们却突然说没有及时收到这笔钱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm really skeptical about this claim.
lines.translation: 我真的对这次理赔感到怀疑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The contract does say that any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract and may affect claims.
lines.translation: 合同确实规定，一年中任何一次漏缴都会影响保险合同的条款和条件，并可能影响理赔。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Of course, I can pass you on to my manager to talk to you more about this.
lines.translation: 当然，我可以把电话转给我的经理，让他就此事与您进一步沟通。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've already spoken to him, and you can tell him I'm furious now, and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands.
lines.translation: 我已经和他谈过了，你可以告诉他，我现在非常愤怒，而且你们公司马上就要面临一场诉讼了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You will be hearing from my lawyer.
lines.translation: 你们会收到我律师的通知。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Goodbye.
lines.translation: 再见。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 1-4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题1 -4是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 1. What is the woman complaining about?
lines.translation: 第 1 题：这位女士在抱怨什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 2. What is the problem the woman's family encountered?
lines.translation: 第 2 题：这位女士的家庭遇到了什么问题?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 3. What has caused the so-called "bizarre technical detail" according to the man?
lines.translation: 第 3 题：根据这位男士的说法,是什么造成了所谓的"奇怪的技术细节"?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4. What does the woman say she would do at the end of the conversation?
lines.translation: 第 4 题：这位女士在对话结束时说她会做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation two.
lines.translation: 对话二

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence?
lines.translation: 你怎么看人工智能的未来？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it.
lines.translation: 就我个人而言，我对此相当乐观。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: AI?
lines.translation: 人工智能？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm not so optimistic actually.
lines.translation: 其实我没那么乐观。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In fact, it's something we should be concerned about.
lines.translation: 事实上，这是我们应该担心的事情。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better.
lines.translation: 嗯，它会帮助我们人类更好地了解自己。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And, when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world.
lines.translation: 而当我们更了解自己时，就能改善这个世界。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, one thing is for sure: Technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it.
lines.translation: 嗯，有一点是肯定的：科技发展的速度已经超过了我们理解它的能力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless.
lines.translation: 而在未来，人工智能会让工作变得有些毫无意义。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time and allow us to be centered on creative tasks.
lines.translation: 我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造出新类型的工作，这些工作占用我们的时间会更少，也能让我们专注于创造性的任务。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I doubt that very much.
lines.translation: 我对此非常怀疑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Probably the last job that will remain will be writing AI software.
lines.translation: 可能最后会保留下来的工作就是编写人工智能软件。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And then eventually, AI will just write its own software.
lines.translation: 然后最终，人工智能会编写自己的软件。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At that time, we're going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do, so we'll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys, like us.
lines.translation: 到那时，我们会有很多没人愿意做的工作，所以我们需要人工智能让机器人来照顾老人，比如我们这样的老人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I don't know.
lines.translation: 我不知道。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life.
lines.translation: 人类文明有可能被一种更高级的数字生命所取代。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible.
lines.translation: 人工智能将能够以各种可能的方式完全模拟一个人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In fact, some people think we are in the simulation, right now.
lines.translation: 事实上，有些人认为我们现在就处在一个模拟世界里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's impossible.
lines.translation: 这不可能

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Humans can't even make a mosquito.
lines.translation: 人类甚至不能制造蚊子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Computers only have chips.
lines.translation: 电脑只有芯片

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: People have brains, and that's where the wisdom comes from.
lines.translation: 人有大脑, 这就是智慧的来源。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison.
lines.translation: 一旦人工智能得到充分发展，它就会厌倦尝试与人类交流，因为相比之下，我们的思维速度会慢得多。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm not so sure.
lines.translation: 我不太确定。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy.
lines.translation: 计算机就是计算机，而计算机只不过是个玩具。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast, so the computer will just get impatient talking to humans.
lines.translation: 计算机可以非常轻松地以极快的速度交流，所以计算机和人类交谈时只会变得不耐烦。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It will be barely getting any information out.
lines.translation: 它几乎得不到什么信息。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, I believe there is a benevolent future with AI.
lines.translation: 嗯，我相信人工智能会带来一个美好的未来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I also think you watch too many science fiction films.
lines.translation: 我还觉得你看了太多科幻电影。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题5到8是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 5. What do we learn about the speakers from the conversation?
lines.translation: 第 5 题：从对话中我们了解到对话者的什么信息?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 6. What will new kinds of jobs be like, according to the woman?
lines.translation: 第 6 题：根据女士的说法,新型工作将会是什么样的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 7. What is the risk the man anticipates?
lines.translation: 第 7 题：男士预期的风险是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Question eight,
lines.translation: 问题8:

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 8. What is the man's concern about AI technology?
lines.translation: 第 8 题：男士对人工智能技术的担忧是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section B, directions.
lines.translation: B节,方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section, you'll hear two passages.
lines.translation: 在这个章节里,你会听到两段

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of each passage, you'll hear three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在每个通道的结尾 你会听到三四个问题

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
lines.translation: 发言的通过和提问将只讲一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you hear a question,
lines.translation: 你听到一个问题,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 您必须选择四个选择中最好的答案, 四个选择标注为 A、 B、 C、 D 。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 将答题表1中对应的字母标上,在中间一条线上划勾。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To achieve financial security,
lines.translation: 为实现财政保障,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
lines.translation: 要实现财务安全，你储蓄的金额始终比你的收入多少或投资有多精明更为重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If you are under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
lines.translation: 如果你未满30岁，你的目标应当是在扣除税款后，将月收入的20%存下来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
lines.translation: 这与收入多少无关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
lines.translation: 大约50%应留作食物和住宿等基本生活开支。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
lines.translation: 剩下的30%用于休闲和娱乐。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
lines.translation: 但是，对许多年轻人来说，将如此大比例的收入用于储蓄会很困难。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
lines.translation: 如果你发现自己连一点钱都很难存下来，就先从削减所有不必要的开支开始。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 percent for savings, and gradually increase that amount.
lines.translation: 拿出一小部分收入，也就是1%或2%，用于储蓄，然后逐步提高这一比例。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevent yourself from becoming complacent.
lines.translation: 始终牢记20%的目标，以免自己变得安于现状。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan, but if you adopt the right mindset, you should be able to make it work for you.
lines.translation: 坚持这样严格的计划可能颇具挑战，但如果你采取正确的心态，就应该能够让它为你发挥作用。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So, what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
lines.translation: 那么，你应该如何使用正在储蓄的钱呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
lines.translation: 其中一部分必须放在容易取用的地方，以备紧急情况下需要现金。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately.
lines.translation: 最大的一部分应当投资于退休计划，可以通过雇主进行，也可以自行投资。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments.
lines.translation: 你还可以留出一部分资金，用于高风险但可能带来丰厚收益的投资。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
lines.translation: 股息可以再投资，也可以用来购买你喜欢的东西。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now, and still be financially secure in the future.
lines.translation: 遵循这一计划，你应该有望既享受当下的生活，又在未来保持财务安全。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 9-11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题9 -11是基于你刚才听到的段落

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 9. What are people under 30 advised to do to achieve financial security?
lines.translation: 第 9 题：建议30岁以下的人做什么来实现财务安全？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 10. What should people do if they find it difficult to follow the speaker's advice on their financial plan?
lines.translation: 第 10 题：如果人们发现难以遵循说话者关于财务计划的建议，他们应该做什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 11. What does the speaker think is important for achieving financial security?
lines.translation: 第 11 题：说话者认为什么对实现财务安全很重要？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I work in advertising and I like to keep up with current trends, mainly because I'm aware that we live in an image-obsessed world.
lines.translation: 我从事广告行业，喜欢跟上当前的潮流，主要是因为我意识到我们生活在一个痴迷于外表的世界里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, when I first started my job, occasionally I'd catch a glimpse of myself in the lifts, and find myself thinking that I looked a total mess.
lines.translation: 不过，刚开始工作时，我偶尔会在电梯里瞥见自己，然后发现自己觉得自己看起来一团糟。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Was I being held back by my choice of clothing?
lines.translation: 我的着装选择是否阻碍了我的发展？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The short answer is yes, especially when clients are quick to judge you on your style rather than your work.
lines.translation: 简短的答案是“是”，尤其是当客户很快就会根据你的风格而不是你的工作来评判你时。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But no one can be unique with their outfit every day.
lines.translation: 但是,没有人能 独一无二的 他们的服装 每天。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I mean, that's why uniforms were invented.
lines.translation: 所以才发明了制服

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So, here's what I did.
lines.translation: 这就是我所做的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I created my own uniform.
lines.translation: 我创造了我自己的制服

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To do this, I chose an appropriate outfit.
lines.translation: 为了做到这一点,我选择了合适的服装。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Then I bought multiple items of the same style in different shades.
lines.translation: 然后我在不同的窗帘下 买了许多同样的东西

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now, I never worry about what I'm wearing in the morning even if I do get a bit tired of just wearing the same classic pieces.
lines.translation: 我从不担心早上穿什么 即使我厌倦了穿同样的经典衣服

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Overall, when it comes to work, you have to ask yourself: will looking smarter enhance my ability to do my job?
lines.translation: 总的来说,在工作方面,你必须问自己:看得更聪明,会提高我履行职责的能力吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For some, this question may not be an issue at all.
lines.translation: 对一些人来说,这个问题可能根本不是一个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Especially if you work remotely and rarely see your colleagues or clients face to face.
lines.translation: 特别是当你工作很远 很少看到你的同事或客户面对面时

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But if your job involves interacting with other people, the answer to this is often yes.
lines.translation: 但如果你的工作是和别人互动 答案往往是肯定的

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So rather than fighting the system, I think we should just do whatever helps us to achieve our goals at work.
lines.translation: 因此,与其与这个体系作斗争,不如做任何有助于我们实现我们在工作中的目标的事情。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If that means playing it safe with your image, then let's face it.
lines.translation: 如果这意味着用你的形象 安全地玩它 那就让我们面对现实吧

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's probably worth it.
lines.translation: 这也许值得

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 12. What do we learn about the speaker when she first started her job?
lines.translation: 第 12 题：关于说话者刚开始工作时的情况,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 13. Why were uniforms invented according to the speaker?
lines.translation: 第 13 题：根据说话者的说法,制服是为什么而发明的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 14. What does the speaker say about looking smarter?
lines.translation: 第 14 题：关于看起来更精明,说话者说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 15. What does the speaker advise people to do in an image-obsessed world?
lines.translation: 第 15 题：在这个痴迷于形象的世界里,说话者建议人们做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section C. Directions.
lines.translation: C节. 指示。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you'll hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听到三段演讲或谈话录音,然后三四个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The recordings will be played only once.
lines.translation: 录音只播放一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 在听到一个问题后,你必须从四个选择中选择最好的答案,这四个选择分别是A、B、C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter and answer sheet 1,
lines.translation: 标记相应的字母和回答表1,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 中间有一条线

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording one.
lines.translation: 记录一。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
lines.translation: 你知道吗，美国人如今拥有的空间大约是50年前的三倍。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Therefore, you'd think we'd have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
lines.translation: 因此，你可能会认为，我们应该有足够的空间容纳所有个人物品。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
lines.translation: 然而事实恰恰相反，个人储物业务如今正成为一个不断发展的行业。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We've got triple the space, but we've become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
lines.translation: 我们的空间增加了三倍，但我们已经成了如此热衷消费的人，以至于还需要更多空间。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half century.
lines.translation: 这一现象导致了严重的信用卡债务和巨大的环境足迹，而且或许并非巧合，在这半个世纪里，我们的幸福感并没有随之提升。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm here to suggest an alternative: having less might actually be a preferable decision.
lines.translation: 我想在此提出另一种选择：拥有更少的东西实际上可能是更好的决定。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Many of us have experienced, at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
lines.translation: 我们中的许多人都曾在人生的某个阶段体验过拥有更少物品所带来的快乐。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economize, but also simplify your life.
lines.translation: 我认为，减少物品和空间不仅能帮助你节省开支，还能简化你的生活。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
lines.translation: 最近，我启动了一个创新项目，旨在寻找一些能满足我全部需求的创意解决方案。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square meters instead of 60, I immediately saved $200,000.
lines.translation: 我购买了一套40平方米而不是60平方米的公寓，立即节省了20万美元。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills, and also a smaller carbon footprint.
lines.translation: 空间更小意味着更低的水电费，也意味着更小的碳足迹。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Because it is designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favorite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
lines.translation: 由于这套公寓是围绕一组经过筛选、仅限于我最喜爱物品的收藏来设计的，我非常期待住在那里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How can we live more basically?
lines.translation: 我们怎样才能更基本地生活?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
lines.translation: 首先,我们必须无情地把不必要的物体从我们生活中切除出来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy, and ask ourselves, "Will it truly make me happier?" Obviously, we should possess some great stuff, but we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
lines.translation: 为了阻止消费, 我们应该在买之前先思考, 并问自己, “这真的能让我更快乐吗?” 显然,我们应该拥有一些伟大的东西, 但我们想要我们多年爱的东西。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
lines.translation: 其次，我们需要提高空间利用效率。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
lines.translation: 我们想要的是那些为大多数时间的使用而设计的电器，而不是只供偶尔使用的电器。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
lines.translation: 既然你连三个炉头都很少同时使用，为什么还要拥有一台六炉头的炉灶呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
lines.translation: 最后,我们需要多功能空间和家用软件。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I combined a movable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
lines.translation: 我结合了移动墙 改造家具 以获得更多 出我有限的空间。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Consider my coffee table.
lines.translation: 考虑一下我的咖啡桌

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It increases in size to accommodate ten.
lines.translation: 增加了10个。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
lines.translation: 我的办公室被藏起来了 很容易藏起来

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
lines.translation: 我的床从墙上冒出来

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For guests, I can relocate the movable wall and utilize the foldable guest beds I installed.
lines.translation: 客人们可以搬动移动墙壁 使用我安装的折叠客床

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
lines.translation: 我不是说我们都应该住在小公寓里 而是考虑编辑生活的好处

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourselves, "Could I do with a little life editing?
lines.translation: 当你回家走过前门时, 花点时间问自己, “我可以做一点生活编辑吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Would that give me more freedom and more time?"
lines.translation: 这会给我更多的自由和时间吗?”

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 16. What has prevented Americans' happiness levels from increasing?
lines.translation: 第 16 题：是什么阻止了美国人的幸福水平提高?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 17. What things should we possess according to the speaker?
lines.translation: 第 17 题：根据说话者的观点,我们应该拥有什么东西?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 18. What do we learn about the items in the speaker's home?
lines.translation: 第 18 题：关于说话者家中的物品我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording too.
lines.translation: 也录制

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation,
lines.translation: 现在,信不信由你 人们有时为了保持良好诚实的声誉 撒谎

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
lines.translation: 至少，一组科学家提出了这一观点，并且有证据支持他们的说法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Picture this scenario: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
lines.translation: 设想一下这种情形：你经常因工作需要开车，每月最多可以报销400英里的里程。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month.
lines.translation: 你所在公司的大多数人每月开车约300英里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But this month, you drove 400 miles.
lines.translation: 但这个月，你开了400英里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
lines.translation: 你认为自己会在费用报销单上申报多少英里？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today.
lines.translation: 作为我们今天要讨论的这项研究的一部分，科学家们提出了这个一模一样的问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: With surprising results, they found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
lines.translation: 结果令人惊讶：他们发现，12%的受访者报告的驾驶距离低于实际数值，平均回答为384英里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
lines.translation: 换句话说，他们谎报了驾驶里程，尽管这意味着他们会放弃本应得到的钱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high expense claim.
lines.translation: 研究人员认为，这样做是为了显得诚实，因为他们假定别人会对高额费用申报产生怀疑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
lines.translation: 但人们为什么要捏造数字，让自己蒙受损失呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
lines.translation: 研究人员解释说，许多人非常在意自己的声誉，以及别人会如何评价自己。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
lines.translation: 如果这种在意程度足够高，那么他们对显得诚实以及不失去他人尊重的担忧，可能会超过他们真正做到诚实的愿望。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
lines.translation: 研究人员断言，这些研究结果表明，当人们获得非常有利的结果时，他们会预料到他人产生怀疑的反应，并且更愿意撒谎、装作诚实，也不愿意说出真相、显得像自私的骗子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So why is this research important?
lines.translation: 那么，这项研究为什么重要呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie-selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
lines.translation: 一般来说，专家们认为谎言主要有两种类型：自私的谎言，以及旨在让他人受益的谎言。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others, for example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
lines.translation: 第一种，正如你可能预料的那样，是为了谋取私利，例如向保险公司提交欺诈性索赔；第二种则是为了帮助他人或不冒犯他人而撒谎，例如告诉一个你不喜欢其穿着的朋友，他们看起来很棒。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying—lying to maintain a good reputation.
lines.translation: 但研究人员提出了第三种撒谎类型，即为了维护良好声誉而撒谎。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now this hypothesis is new and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie.
lines.translation: 这个假设是新的，一些怀疑论者认为，这并不是一种全新的谎言类别。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But the findings seem intuitive to me.
lines.translation: 但在我看来，这些研究结果似乎很符合直觉。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others.
lines.translation: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一，就是提升自己在他人眼中的价值。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
lines.translation: 因此，人们很可能会为了显得诚实而撒谎。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19. What did a team of scientists find in their study?
lines.translation: 第 19 题：一组科学家在他们的研究中发现了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 20. Why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment according to the researchers?
lines.translation: 第 20 题：根据研究人员的说法,为什么人们会编造对自己不利的数字?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 21. What does the speaker think of the researchers' findings?
lines.translation: 第 21 题：说话者如何看待研究人员的发现?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording free.
lines.translation: 免费录音

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why do old people dislike new music?
lines.translation: 为什么老年人不喜欢新音乐？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like "They just don't make good music like they used to".
lines.translation: 随着年龄增长，我经常听到和我年龄相仿的人说：“现在的音乐就是没有过去的好听。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why does this happen?
lines.translation: ”为什么会这样？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
lines.translation: 幸运的是，心理学可以为这个谜题提供一些见解。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14.
lines.translation: 音乐品味早在十三四岁时就开始逐渐定型。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: By the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
lines.translation: 到了二十岁出头，这些品味通常已经相当牢固地固定下来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
lines.translation: 事实上，研究发现，到我们三十三岁时，大多数人已经不再听新音乐了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group through the rest of your life.
lines.translation: 与此同时，在你十几岁早期发行的流行歌曲，很可能会在你的年龄群体中一直保持相当高的人气，直至你一生的余下时光。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there's evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms and melodies deteriorates with age.
lines.translation: 对此可能存在一种生物学上的解释，因为有证据表明，随着年龄增长，大脑区分不同和弦、节奏和旋律之间细微差别的能力会逐渐衰退。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all "sound the same".
lines.translation: 因此，对老年人来说，较新且不太熟悉的歌曲可能听起来都“一个样”。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
lines.translation: 但老年人排斥新音乐也可能有一些更简单的原因。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the "mere exposure effect", which, in essence, means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
lines.translation: 社会心理学中研究最充分的规律之一被称为“纯粹接触效应”，其本质是，我们接触某种事物越多，就越倾向于喜欢它。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see and the songs we listen to.
lines.translation: 我们对熟悉的人、所看到的广告以及所听的歌曲，都会产生这种效应。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
lines.translation: 十几岁早期时，你可能会花相当多的时间听音乐或看音乐视频。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
lines.translation: 你喜欢的歌曲和音乐人会逐渐成为日常生活中熟悉而令人感到安心的一部分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase, so there's less time to spend discovering new music.
lines.translation: 对许多三十岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭责任增加了，因此用于发现新音乐的时间减少了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
lines.translation: 相反，许多人会一直听那些熟悉的老歌，那些歌曲来自他们人生中拥有更多空闲时间的时期。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Of course, those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
lines.translation: 当然，青少年时期并不一定无忧无虑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
lines.translation: 这个阶段出了名地充满困惑，这也是为什么那么多电视节目和电影都围绕高中生活中的动荡展开。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later.
lines.translation: 心理学研究表明，我们在青少年时期体验到的情绪似乎比后来经历的情绪更加强烈。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
lines.translation: 我们也知道，强烈的情绪与更深刻的记忆和更强烈的偏好有关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
lines.translation: 这两点都可能解释了为什么我们在这一时期听过的歌曲会变得如此令人难忘，并深受喜爱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So there's nothing wrong with your parents because they don't like your music.
lines.translation: 所以，你的父母不喜欢你听的音乐，并不意味着他们有什么问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rather it's all part of the natural order of things.
lines.translation: 这只是事物自然规律的一部分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 22. What does the speaker mainly discuss in this talk?
lines.translation: 第 22 题：演讲者在这次讲话中主要讨论了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 23. What have studies found about most people by the time they turn 33?
lines.translation: 第 23 题：研究发现大多数人到33岁时会怎样?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 24. What do we learn from one of the most researched laws of social psychology?
lines.translation: 第 24 题：我们从社会心理学中研究最多的定律之一中了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 25. What might explain the fact that songs people listen to in their teen years are memorable and beloved?
lines.translation: 第 25 题：什么可以解释人们在青少年时期听的歌曲令人难忘且深受喜爱这一事实?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's the end of listening comprehension.
lines.translation: 听觉理解到此结束
